summary:
# NOTES: THE RUNAWAYS (Nat Gould). Single book, 20 chapters.

## Front matter
- Publisher: G. Heath Robinson & J. Birch Ltd, London. Printed by William Clowes & Sons.
- Appreciation by E. Laton Blacklands. Gould b. Manchester 1857, d. 1919. Journalist in England and Australia. Hobbies: racing, driving, gardening. Times obit quote: "a rattling good story makes a reader happier and more contented."
- Back ads: Royal Ascot Library (The Runaways listed as "Now on sale"); *Out and Away* magazine.

## Characters
- **Redmond Maynard**: Squire, Hazelwell. Tall (~6ft), proud, honourable, strong. Sits up every anniversary of Ulick's leaving.
- **Ulick Maynard**: son. Quarrel two years before: father accused him of wronging Janet Todd. Ulick: "Believing, as you must... I will no longer inflict my presence upon you, sir. Good-night." Left that night; never returned to Hazelwell until reconciliation.
- **Bersak**: Ulick's wolf-hound. Saved Ulick from a 3-yr-old bull. Guards Squire.
- **Irene Courtly** (née Carstone): daughter of Colonel Carstone (old friend of Squire). Squire's ward from age 16. Painter, skilled rider. Married Warren ~6 months after Ulick left. Loves Ulick; not Warren.
- **Warren Courtly**: Irene's husband, Anselm Manor. Gambler, jealous of Random, unfaithful. Seduced Janet, took her away the night of Ulick's quarrel. Sold Holme Farm £10,000. Dies in Ch XIX.
- **Eli Todd**: Hazelwell stud manager. Ex-Hussar with Colonel Carstone (India, Walers, Viceroy's Cup second with "Scout"). Devoted to Ulick, believes him innocent.
- **Janet Todd**: Eli's daughter. Pretty, vain flirt. Ran off with Warren; lived at Feltham as "Mrs. Warren."
- **Mary Marley**: Irene's maid. Bob Heather's sweetheart.
- **Mrs. Marley**: Eli's housekeeper (different person).
- **Bob Heather**: Hazelwell groom/driver, "the tub."
- **Martha Dixon**: Anselm Manor housekeeper. Stern, loves Irene.
- **Felix Hoffman**: racecourse tout, sharper, blackmailer. Jewish features, black curly hair, fierce moustache, shifty brown eyes.
- **Mrs. Hoffman**: Felix's mother, 25 Main Street, Feltham. Husband Milas Hoffman, travelling jeweller/swindler, deserted her.
- **Fred May**: trainer, Stanton House, Newmarket. Trained Honeysuckle.
- **Ben Sprig**: jockey, tiny, solemn, bronze face, "the saints be praised."
- **Dr. Harding**: Squire's doctor, old friend.
- **James (Jim) Bard**: vet, Helton.
- **Joe**: stud lad. **Old Josh**: publican.
- **Sam Lane**: Rushshire huntsman (earlier). Unnamed huntsman later.
- **Conrad Rush**: owner of Kit Cat.
- **Dyer**: jockey on Milander.
- **Harewood**: name on vault in Glen church churchyard.
- **Vicar and wife**: at final dinner.

## Horses
- **Random**: bright bay, Ulick's favourite hunter. Squire gave to Irene on marriage. Irene painted him; gave painting to Squire.
- **Rupert**: Irene's dark brown mount.
- **Honeysuckle**: old mare (Squire says 18, Eli says 20). Won Oaks and St Leger for Squire. Foaled colt ~quarter hour after midnight, New Year's Day, as Helton church bells rang. Colt later won Jockey Club Stakes (trained by Fred May).
- **The Saint**: grey, "washy"/flea-bitten, by Father Confessor out of Hilda. Runs as "Mr. Lanark." Owned by Ulick, bought for 200 guineas via Fred May at Lowland Lodge, Epsom. Called "the curiosity."
- **Bersak's rival**: Blossom (mare in Eli's box, mentioned).
- Others: Scout, Buchanan, Milander, Sandstone (Derby winner), Pinkerton, Kit Cat, Mulgar, Ringbell.

## Places
- Hazelwell (Squire's house), Helton (village, church clock), Haydon Station, Hazelwell Coppice, Hazelwell Spinney, Brecon Wood, Glen church, river Tone.
- Anselm Manor: former monastery; Henry VIII gift deed to Anselm Courtly; Holme Farm.
- Feltham (Mrs. Hoffman; near Hanworth Park, Windsor line). Kempton Park. Hurst Park. Newmarket (Stanton House). Epsom (Lowland Lodge, Tattersall's). The Walton Hotel (London, by Embankment). Ulick's flat: West Kensington.

## Plot, in order

**Ch I (snow, anniversary night):** Squire at window. Recalls quarrel. Irene arrives on foot in lace-up boots; Warren "gone to London." Squire has Bob fetch Mary Marley and luggage. Irene asks if she should stay. Squire says he'll sit up all night, expecting Ulick.

**Ch II:** Eli's background. Ulick had recommended him. Janet's night: Ulick visited Eli's cottage, talked with Janet; next morning she was gone. Squire storms to Eli, accuses Ulick. Eli: "I'd cut off my right hand first." Eli walks out, sees Bob passing with "the tub"; Bob drinks Eli's ale.

**Ch III:** Squire dozes; Bersak guards. Bersak's bull story. Squire's morning musings on Warren, Irene, Ulick. Breakfast; Irene says Random painting is done. Anselm Manor history. Warren jealous of Random.

**Ch IV:** Irene rides Rupert to Anselm with painting strapped on back. Meets Eli at stud: Honeysuckle foaling worry; asks no word to Squire. Eli: "he'll have to look to himself" re man who took Janet. At Anselm: Warren's brief letter ("et cetera"; scented paper). Felix Hoffman's begging letter (25 Main Street, Feltham). Irene sends £5 cheque. Dixon: Irene asks letters be forwarded.

**Ch V (New Year's Eve, then midnight):** Eli frantic over Honeysuckle. Ulick arrives at stud unseen. Talk: Eli reveals Janet left the same night. Eli hints suspect is someone dear to Squire. Colt born after midnight. Ulick reveals he owns the Saint as "Mr. Lanark." Gives London address. Walks to Haydon Station.

**Ch VI:** Feltham; Felix's background. Milas Hoffman's fraud. Felix: tout, bookmaker partner, then own losing book. Warren meets Felix at Hurst Park re Milander (5/1); gives Dyer £10. Warren brings Janet to Mrs. Hoffman's as "Mrs. Warren," £3 a week. Warren marries Irene 7–8 months later. Janet threatens to tell Irene; allowance agreed.

**Ch VII:** Felix reads Warren's letter, learns name. Writes begging letter to Irene (gets £5). Irene shows Squire both letters; Squire forbids more money. New Year's Day: Eli reports foal; walk to stud; Squire admires colt. Irene reads paper: Holme Farm sold £10,000. Squire says worth £5,000 more. Warren visits Janet; she demands £20 and threatens; he pays.

**Ch VIII:** Warren home; admits selling Holme Farm to pay gambling debts. Thaw. Felix's letter reaches Irene; Warren goes white at the signature. Warren visits Hazelwell; Squire presses him; Warren lies. Felix's second letter returns £5 with thanks; Warren uneasy.

**Ch IX:** Ulick in London. Christmas in city; boy & girl in Trafalgar Square, given 10 shillings. Spring: Epsom, City & Suburban. Meets Fred May. Fred has the Saint (grey, two-year-old, 200 gns). Ulick buys him, leaves him with Fred. Saint wins four races as two-year-old. Ulick resolves to find Janet.

**Ch X:** Pastures Handicap, Kempton Park (mile, £500). Saint 8st vs Pinkerton 8st12 (dangerous). Kit Cat (Conrad Rush, 7st) favourite-ish; Mulgar, Ringbell. Ben Sprig rides; squeezes through on rails when Kit Cat bores out. Wins by ~3/4 length; Pinkerton 2nd; Kit Cat 3rd. Friend drives Ulick to Feltham; Ulick spots Janet in street.

**Ch XI:** Ulick at Janet's door (Mrs. Hoffman out). Janet pleads; Ulick promises to write Eli that she's well but keep address secret. Warren arrives; Ulick hidden in kitchen as "Mr. Hazelwell." Ulick sees Warren's shame; resolves Irene must never know. Mrs. Hoffman flirts with Ulick; her rambling. Janet says Warren "promised to marry me when I ran off with him."

**Ch XII:** Squire's decline; Dr. Harding urges travel; Irene persuades Squire to go south. Eli writes Ulick begging return; Ulick refuses ("circumstances might arise"). Eli writes Fred May. Fred agrees to plot. Ulick at Newmarket for "buyer." Squire and Eli arrive at Stanton House. Father and son reunite. Squire: "I will trust you, my son." Ulick refuses to come home yet.

**Ch XIII:** Squire, Eli, Fred celebrate with champagne. Squire sees the Saint: "What a horrible colour!" Squire wants to buy; Ulick refuses. Squire asks Eli if he knows who ran off with Janet. Train home: Squire says Warren sold Holme Farm. Dinner at Walton Hotel with Warren and Irene. Balcony talk: Irene admits she thought Ulick guilty; Eli told her Ulick left first. Warren: "I have an excellent reason."

**Ch XIV:** Squire quarrels with Warren. Felix blackmails Warren for £50 (threat: tell Irene of "Mrs. Warren"). Warren pays. Felix loses, asks Warren for more; Warren refuses, says he's told his wife everything. Felix writes Irene: £100, address of "Mrs. Warren" at his mother's house. Irene sends £100; goes to Feltham; meets Mrs. Hoffman, who says Warren rarely comes.

**Ch XV:** Irene meets Janet, who admits everything. Janet: "If there be any wrong, you did it to me." Janet says Ulick forbade her to reveal (for Irene's sake). Irene plans to keep it secret; advises Janet to return to Eli; Janet refuses. Irene: forbid Warren the house. Irene returns to Walton; Warren angry at her unannounced trip. Ulick calls; Irene invites him to dinner. Warren sneers; Irene threatens to retaliate.

**Ch XVI:** Warren losing at bridge and racing; Anselm in danger. Dinner: Warren rude; Ulick glares. Ulick tells Warren he owns the Saint. Warren plans big bet on Saint if Sandstone wins Derby (Sandstone does). Squire receives Fred May's letter about the Saint. Coronation Cup, Epsom, Derby week: Vulture (American, stars & stripes, Derby & St Leger, crouching jockey, temperamental), Coralie (purple & scarlet, Ascot Gold Cup), Avenger (yellow/red cap, Cesarewitch), Decoy Duck (Eclipse), Mermaid (Oaks). Saint 8/1. Squire bets £200; Irene a "pony"; Fred May and Ben £50 each. Ben boxes Saint late, rides race; Saint beats Vulture by a short head after duel.

**Ch XVII:** Felix in paddock, lost £100 on Vulture; asks Warren for tenner. Warren refuses, threatens. Felix: "I'll go straight to your wife... she's here." Warren raises fist; Squire stops it. Felix: "You have two [wives]"; hands card with address. Warren tears card; Squire takes second card. Warren denies; Squire doubts. Warren strikes Felix, knocks him down. Squire: "It served him right." Irene begs Squire drop the matter. Warren telegraphs Janet to flee. A week later at Anselm, Warren confesses to Irene about Janet; Irene reveals she knows all, from Janet. Warren threatens to sell Anselm and leave with her if she tells Squire; threatens to harm Ulick. Irene: "I love him"; Warren rides off wildly; returns late; Irene softens.

**Ch XVIII (next hunting season):** Rushshire hounds meet at Hazelwell. Ulick writes Eli to host him; wants to ride Random. Irene lends Random to Eli "for a friend." Ulick at stud; sees Random; Eli says Ulick won't return until the man confesses to Squire. Ulick: Janet is well, won't come home yet. Ulick stays at Bard's house in Helton. Squire has gout (Dr. Harding), absent. Hunt to Brecon Wood; fox runs; Tone river crossing via fallen tree. Warren on Irish grey sees Ulick on Random; enraged. Huntsman's comment on Janet. Fox runs into Glen church churchyard. Ulick goes round; Warren dares him over wall.

**Ch XIX:** Warren jumps wall; grey catches hind legs; falls on raised slab (Harewood's vault). Warren's neck broken; dies. Grey dead. Ulick checks body, covers face. Meets Squire and Irene walking; says Warren fell. Irene rushes to churchyard; sees body; faints on it. Squire carries her; Dr. Harding confirms death. Carriage to Anselm; Irene: "I want to be there with him alone." Warren buried in Anselm church vault. Ulick and Squire discuss the leap. Janet reads of death; returns to Eli; writes asking forgiveness; Eli welcomes her. Eli: "Who induced you...?" Janet: "Warren Courtly." Eli: "I thought as much."

**Ch XX (a year later, anniversary):** Squire and Ulick in morning room. Dinner party: Irene, Dr. Harding, Vicar & wife. Squire & Vicar's wife vs Vicar & Dr. Harding at whist. Ulick proposes to Irene in drawing room while she sings. She accepts. Squire: "Not had one yet?" Irene: "Dozens." Squire recalls sitting up on this same night. Wedding in summer; abroad; then Anselm Manor. Irene knows all re Janet and Warren; Squire knows facts. Janet becomes Irene's lady's maid after Mary Marley and Bob Heather marry. Irene's son born; Squire's grandson (named Ulick, "young Ulick"). Squire "grown young." Honeysuckle's son wins Jockey Club Stakes. The Saint's foals; Ulick wants a grey. Felix flees country after police trouble. Janet sends gifts to Mrs. Hoffman. Ulick's occasional memory of Warren's leap. Ends: "THE END."
